From fa3c411d21ebc26ffd175c7256c37cefa35020aa Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Tetsuo Handa <penguin-kernel@I-love.SAKURA.ne.jp>
Date: Sat, 20 Dec 2025 11:11:33 +0900
Subject: [PATCH] RDMA/core: always drop device refcount in
 ib_del_sub_device_and_put()

Since nldev_deldev() (introduced by commit 060c642b2ab8 ("RDMA/nldev: Add
support to add/delete a sub IB device through netlink") grabs a reference
using ib_device_get_by_index() before calling ib_del_sub_device_and_put(),
we need to drop that reference before returning -EOPNOTSUPP error.

Reported-by: syzbot+881d65229ca4f9ae8c84@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Closes: https://syzkaller.appspot.com/bug?extid=881d65229ca4f9ae8c84
Fixes: bca51197620a ("RDMA/core: Support IB sub device with type "SMI"")
Signed-off-by: Tetsuo Handa <penguin-kernel@I-love.SAKURA.ne.jp>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/80749a85-cbe2-460c-8451-42516013f9fa@I-love.SAKURA.ne.jp
Reviewed-by: Parav Pandit <parav@nvidia.com>
Signed-off-by: Leon Romanovsky <leon@kernel.org>

diff --git a/drivers/infiniband/core/device.c b/drivers/infiniband/core/device.c
index 13e8a1714bbd..1174ab7da629 100644
--- a/drivers/infiniband/core/device.c
+++ b/drivers/infiniband/core/device.c
@@ -2881,8 +2881,10 @@ int ib_del_sub_device_and_put(struct ib_device *sub)
 {
 	struct ib_device *parent = sub->parent;
 
-	if (!parent)
+	if (!parent) {
+		ib_device_put(sub);
 		return -EOPNOTSUPP;
+	}
 
 	mutex_lock(&parent->subdev_lock);
 	list_del(&sub->subdev_list);
-- 
2.34.1

The patch modifies the function `ib_del_sub_device_and_put()` in `drivers/infiniband/core/device.c` to ensure the device reference count is properly decremented before returning an error. Specifically, when the `parent` pointer is `NULL`, the function previously returned `-EOPNOTSUPP` without releasing the reference obtained by the caller (`nldev_deldev()` via `ib_device_get_by_index()`). The fix adds a call to `ib_device_put(sub)` inside the `if (!parent)` block, dropping the reference before the early return. This prevents a reference leak and resolves a syzbot-reported issue. The change is isolated to a single file and addresses the missing `ib_device_put()` in that error path.

Here is the commit message:
RDMA/core: always drop device refcount in
 ib_del_sub_device_and_put()

Since nldev_deldev() (introduced by commit 060c642b2ab8 ("RDMA/nldev: Add
support to add/delete a sub IB device through netlink") grabs a reference
using ib_device_get_by_index() before calling ib_del_sub_device_and_put(),
we need to drop that reference before returning -EOPNOTSUPP error.

Reported-by: syzbot+881d65229ca4f9ae8c84@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Closes: https://syzkaller.appspot.com/bug?extid=881d65229ca4f9ae8c84
Fixes: bca51197620a ("RDMA/core: Support IB sub device with type "SMI"")
Signed-off-by: Tetsuo Handa <penguin-kernel@I-love.SAKURA.ne.jp>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/80749a85-cbe2-460c-8451-42516013f9fa@I-love.SAKURA.ne.jp
Reviewed-by: Parav Pandit <parav@nvidia.com>
Signed-off-by: Leon Romanovsky <leon@kernel.org>

Here is the root cause:
In `ib_del_sub_device_and_put()`, when the device has no parent (`parent == NULL`), the function returns `-EOPNOTSUPP` without calling `ib_device_put(sub)` to drop the reference that was previously acquired by the caller (`nldev_deldev()` via `ib_device_get_by_index()`). This causes a reference count leak, leading to improper device lifecycle management and potential use-after-free or resource exhaustion.

Here is the patch:
 
 int ib_del_sub_device_and_put(struct ib_device *sub)
 {
 	struct ib_device *parent = sub->parent;
 
-	if (!parent)
+	if (!parent) {
+		ib_device_put(sub);
 		return -EOPNOTSUPP;
+	}
 
 	mutex_lock(&parent->subdev_lock);
 	list_del(&sub->subdev_list);
 	mutex_unlock(&parent->subdev_lock);
 
 	ib_device_put(sub);
 	parent->ops.del_sub_dev(sub);
 	ib_device_put(parent);
 
 	return 0;
 }
 EXPORT_SYMBOL(ib_del_sub_device_and_put);
